summary:
Space Aura is a junior simulator that shows the different phases of a space mission whose aim is to arrive at the moon and the different problems that may arise in each part of the journey. This project is made comprehensible for the general public because its main objective is to give users a general overview in a gamified way that makes learning more entertaining.

The simulation uses a 2D pixel art style that evokes the classical games of the 1990s. This choice makes it easy to develop a clear storyline while keeping a user friendly interface and a showy aesthetic.
details:
The main objective of the simulation is to give an overview of how a space mission to the moon looks like to the general public. This is done through a series of minigames that explain what obstacles astronauts have to face in the launching, the trip to the moon, what things have to be done once they land to the moon and simulate the landing of the space shuttle.

The game is built in Godot 4 with GDScript, as one scene per stage. Two autoloads carry the mission between scenes: Mission stores the chosen spacecraft, the budget and the score, and Global stores the spacecraft's integrity. Web build: the game is exported to HTML5 and embedded in the project website, so it runs in any modern browser with no install.

This project is creative because it is a fun and interactive way to learn about space missions, a subject that is usually dense even for adults. This is also optimized so that anyone can access it in any device they want. We even took into consideration the language, impementing an English and a Spanish version.

For more details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GOx5GZj7lNeJb19KyF5KnPXd-vSFCisCeJ5lyO7I_n4/edit?usp=sharing
